title: Cumberland Falls

bodyMarkdown:
Where the Cumberland crosses the hard Lower Pennsylvanian Rockcastle conglomerate, softer rock below erodes faster and keeps a ~68-foot, 125-foot-wide drop, the “Niagara of the South.” The falls likely began near the Pottsville Escarpment by Burnside and retreated about 45 miles upstream, cutting the gorge.

On clear full-moon nights the mist throws a moonbow. It is the only place in the Western Hemisphere where moonbows are known to appear with regularity.

In the late 1920s a hydroelectric plan threatened the falls, and T. Coleman du Pont offered to buy the falls and surrounding land to save them, but he died before the purchase. In 1930 his widow completed the purchase and the family gave the land to Kentucky. The state park opened in 1931.
Source: [Cumberland Falls (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cumberland_Falls)
